destinations.summary: Keeps the correlator construction, equation-of-motion consistency and noncritical-string consequences within one formal-theory question.

destinations.title: Shared-scalar determination from overlapping string species
destinations.question: Can consistency among overlapping strings with different integration constants determine a shared scalar that a single species cannot determine?
destinations.summary: Organizes the multispecies consistency mechanism without assigning the scalar an unsupported cosmological role.

destinations.title: Reflecting-wall spectral scales and string-backreaction horizon models
destinations.question: How does radial localization set probe-scalar spectral hierarchies near a reflecting wall, and can classical-string backreaction delay the spectral-form-factor dip so that the effective model better approximates horizon dynamics?
destinations.summary: Links radial spectral organization to a distinct backreaction-induced dip-time test in one effective horizon model.

destinations.title: String-ensemble statistics for particle properties and vacuum energy
destinations.question: Can large ensembles of string solutions produce useful particle-property distributions or a statistical account of a small cosmological constant?
destinations.summary: Preserves the two uses of a common string ensemble without reducing particle phenomenology to cosmological-constant selection.

destinations.title: Field-theory cosmic strings: classification, formation, evolution and observations
destinations.question: Which field theories support cosmic strings, how do those strings form and evolve cosmologically, and can their gravitational and other interactions produce distinguishable observational signatures?
destinations.summary: A composite review home retains the full chain from supporting field theories through cosmological dynamics to observations.

destinations.title: Quintessential inflation with scalar survival and dissipative reheating
destinations.question: Can a single surviving scalar drive inflation and present dark energy while dissipation reheats the universe without requiring inflaton decay?
destinations.summary: Treats inflation, reheating and late dark energy as one coupled scalar-survival problem.

destinations.title: Warm inflation: background dynamics, control and primordial predictions
destinations.question: Under what source-specific background, interaction and perturbation conditions can dissipative inflation be sustained and produce the required primordial fluctuations while satisfying its stated construction and reheating requirements?
destinations.summary: A joint model-evaluation region connects sustained inflation, source-specific control and primordial predictions while preserving distinct kinetic sectors, gravitational settings, approximations and observational dates.

destinations.title: Equilibrium black-hole charge fluctuations and proposed topology avoidance
destinations.question: Is a zero-mean-charge black hole in thermal equilibrium stable against charge fluctuations, what determines their variance, and can an intrinsic fluctuation explain proposed topology avoidance when charged particles are absorbed?
destinations.summary: Keeps equilibrium stability, charge variance and the proposed intrinsic-fluctuation explanation of topology avoidance together as one source-scoped compound question.

destinations.title: Einstein-compatible matter flows and light-state interpretations
destinations.question: Can action-induced geometric flows of gravity coupled to matter preserve Einstein equations, and can the additional matter needed for compatibility support proposed light-state interpretations or a dynamical extension of swampland distance ideas?
destinations.summary: A composite scope joining equation compatibility with explicitly proposed extra-matter and light-state interpretations. The earlier compatibility question and the later dynamical-distance question remain distinct immutable source questions; shared placement establishes no fine equivalence.

destinations.title: Wormhole flow stability and integrability implications
destinations.question: Do asymptotically flat wormhole spatial geometries remain stable under long-time Ricci flow and perturbative two-loop corrections, or develop throat singularities, and what might this imply for sigma-model integrability?
destinations.summary: Preserves the joint stability and possible-integrability question. Earlier apparent stability is tested, perturbative corrections retain their limited regime, and any integrability inference requires evidence beyond the geometric-flow outcome.

destinations.title: DESI evolution across string-inspired and interacting scenarios
destinations.question: Which source-specified string-inspired quintessence and interacting dark-sector scenarios can accommodate the reported DESI preference for evolving dark energy while satisfying the proposed quantum-gravity criteria?
destinations.summary: A whole scenario-comparison question that retains both model classes without assuming a shared scalar realization or coupling law.

destinations.title: Quintessence–IDM inflation, late acceleration and refined-conjecture tests
destinations.question: Can the exponentially coupled quintessence–IDM framework support observationally viable inflation and effective late-time acceleration, and can its curved field space and multifield dynamics alleviate refined de Sitter Swampland tension?
destinations.summary: A model-specific composite question joining two cosmological epochs to the framework's conditional refined-conjecture test.

destinations.title: DESI DR2 quintom-B histories and future TCC compatibility
destinations.question: Which source-specified dynamical-dark-energy parameterizations and selected modified-gravity models can satisfy DESI DR2-motivated quintom-B evolution together with the TCC, including its restrictions on their future evolution?
destinations.summary: A cross-model consistency question retaining phenomenological histories, modified-gravity alternatives and future-evolution conditions.

destinations.title: GMGHS capture, hoop protection and merger-entropy bounds
destinations.question: Can charged test-particle capture destroy a GMGHS dilaton black hole, can the proposed hoop treatment protect censorship, and does entropy increase in the proposed merger impose a weak-gravity-type charge-to-mass condition?
destinations.summary: A single compound question covering the specified capture experiment, its hoop-based treatment and a distinct merger-entropy constraint.

destinations.title: Analytic bootstrap constraints and research directions
destinations.question: How do symmetry, causality, unitarity and OPE consistency constrain strongly coupled CFTs and AdS gravitational UV completions, and which open problems guide analytic bootstrap methods?
destinations.summary: A survey-level home joining CFT constraints and solution strategies, gravitational UV-completion tests in AdS, and future analytic-bootstrap directions while preserving their distinct targets and hypotheses.

destinations.title: Six-dimensional self-tuning and radiative vacuum energy
destinations.question: Can classical self-tuning in six-dimensional supergravity cancel large brane vacuum energies and remain stable enough under quantum corrections to leave four-dimensional energy density of order 1/r^4?
destinations.summary: A composite question about classical brane-vacuum-energy cancellation and quantum stability of the residual four-dimensional energy. No AdS-to-dS uplift is specified.

destinations.title: ANN+GA flux critical-point statistics
destinations.question: How do potential values and other features vary across the ANN+GA critical-point sample, comparing its two flux cases while retaining both AdS and dS points without imposing stability?
destinations.summary: A statistical characterization of the stated search sample, distinct from constructing only stable vacua or certifying the full flux landscape.

destinations.title: Finite-amplitude selection of primordial Weyl curvature
destinations.question: Can finite-amplitude selection explain small primordial Weyl curvature?
destinations.summary: A primordial-geometry and initial-condition selection question whose selection formalism and observational consequences are not specified in the supplied description.

destinations.title: Two-stream magnetogenesis and polarization tests in GRB shocks
destinations.question: Can an anisotropy-driven relativistic two-stream instability generate the magnetic fields required in internal GRB shocks and external afterglow shocks, and can polarization scintillations test this mechanism?
destinations.summary: Keeps field generation in both GRB shock environments and its proposed polarization-scintillation diagnostic within one compound question.

destinations.title: Coupled inflaton, expansion, and strongly interacting matter history
destinations.question: Can a dynamical inflaton and expanding spacetime be coupled self-consistently to strongly interacting matter, producing inflation, reheating and eventual thermal QFT domination?
destinations.summary: A complete coupled-history question preserving the specific thermal-QFT endpoint without assuming a radiation equation of state or an equilibrium bath during inflation.

destinations.title: Graph spectra, candidate string geometry and dynamical claims
destinations.question: Can finite graph spectra canonically generate algebraic curves supporting topological recursion, continuum geometry and string partition functions, and do the proposed bridges support unitary scattering and resolution of BKL spacelike singularities?
destinations.summary: One composite question assessing a proposed spectral construction and its additional physical claims, with qualified or insufficiently specified bridges retained explicitly.

destinations.title: Einstein–Gauss–Bonnet branch stability and instanton tests
destinations.question: Are the two Einstein–Gauss–Bonnet vacua stable despite positive spherical-black-hole masses, and what can vacuum-transition and black-hole-production instantons establish when perturbation theory becomes strongly coupled?
destinations.summary: Connects branch stability, black-hole mass diagnostics and two instanton tests while preserving their different implications and limits.

destinations.title: Bosonic flux AdS, tachyon stability and thermal spectra
destinations.question: Can added form flux support a tachyon-stable nonsupersymmetric bosonic AdS background and a conjectural boundary CFT, and how should its finite-temperature scalar spectra be interpreted as candidate glueballs?
destinations.summary: Preserves the bosonic-string construction, restricted stability test, candidate holographic description and thermal spectral interpretation in one question.

destinations.title: Single-species leptogenesis in a Kalb–Ramond torsion background
destinations.question: Can a prescribed string-inspired Kalb–Ramond torsion background supply CP and CPT violation that generates a lepton asymmetry through tree-level heavy-Majorana-neutrino decays with only one right-handed species?
destinations.summary: A complete home for the background-driven asymmetry question, keeping the heavy-neutrino mass as an ingredient rather than a mass-generation target.

destinations.title: Horizontal alignment, supersymmetric CP and μ-term viability
destinations.question: Can Abelian horizontal symmetries align quarks and squarks and suppress dangerous supersymmetric CP violation while retaining an order-one CKM phase, realistic quark hierarchies and a viable μ term in the same construction?
destinations.summary: A composite flavour-model feasibility question preserving every simultaneous requirement without importing a strong-CP solution.

destinations.title: Type 0’B dark bubbles: scale separation, particle physics and cosmology
destinations.question: Can D3-branes in nonsupersymmetric type 0’B string theory realize a scale-separated dark bubble with viable particle physics, inflation and late-time acceleration?
destinations.summary: Preserves the joint construction and viability question, including particle physics independently of the cosmological epochs.

destinations.title: Extra-natural B−L inflation, particle physics and restricted reheating
destinations.question: Can extra-natural inflation based on gauged U(1)_(B−L) link inflationary observables to particle physics with brane-localized Standard Model fields, and how do restricted inflaton decay channels determine reheating?
destinations.summary: A whole-model question joining higher-dimensional gauge inflation, matter localization and decay-controlled reheating.

destinations.title: Standard Model compactification vacua and conditional neutrino implications
destinations.question: Which lower-dimensional vacua arise from compactifying the Standard Model, how stable are they, and what conditional implications follow for nonsupersymmetric AdS conjectures and neutrino parameters from multiple point criticality?
destinations.summary: Combines vacuum classification and stability with the distinct conditional conjecture and neutrino-criticality questions.

destinations.title: Tower, modulus and decay tests of scale-separated effective AdS
destinations.question: Can scale-separated effective AdS solutions satisfy proposed quantum-gravity conditions on towers, light moduli and nonsupersymmetric decay?
destinations.summary: A composite consistency question preserving three distinct conditional tests in the same effective-AdS setting.

destinations.title: Indirect quantum-gravity tests of AdS5 hierarchies and dS5 descriptions
destinations.question: Can quantum-gravity constraints obstruct scale separation in supersymmetric AdS5 and trustworthy effective descriptions of dS5 without assuming conjectures that directly forbid those vacua?
destinations.summary: Retains the paired five-dimensional AdS and dS targets and their restriction to indirect consistency arguments.

destinations.title: Profiled IIB AdS reduction to effective dS and strong-ADC spectral evidence
destinations.question: Can circle reduction of a higher-dimensional type IIB AdS vacuum with a nonconstant metric profile yield a four-dimensional low-energy de Sitter effective vacuum, and can its KK spectrum provide bottom-up evidence for the strong AdS distance conjecture?
destinations.summary: Keeps the reduction outcome and the associated spectral conjecture test in one source-specific question.

destinations.title: Coupling histograms, α-state probabilities and Euclidean gravity
destinations.question: How does a chosen coupling histogram determine α-state probabilities and the Euclidean gravitational prescription?
destinations.summary: A probability-measure question whose input is a chosen coupling histogram and whose outputs include state probabilities and a gravitational prescription.

destinations.title: Oscillator vacuum information distance at both frequency limits
destinations.question: Why do both vanishing and infinite oscillator frequency produce infinite vacuum information distance?
destinations.summary: Preserves the comparison of the two oscillator-frequency limits as one vacuum information-geometry question.

destinations.title: Long-range SYK dynamics and protected boundary operator data
destinations.question: How do long-range disorder correlations affect spectra, chaos and spatial scrambling in the specified solvable SYK-like fixed points, and what operator data can be protected in the related boundary Yukawa-SYK construction by its free higher-dimensional bulk?
destinations.summary: A composite question preserving the source's two constructions: two-dimensional long-range dynamics and three-dimensional boundary operator data coupled to a four-dimensional free bulk. Their dimensions, observables and protection mechanisms remain distinct.

relations.title: Does the produced population have the assumed subsequent cascade?
relations.rationale: Adequate initial production does not establish cascade efficiency. Check the background and couplings before applying the reported threshold scaling.

relations.title: What flat-model bounds follow from suppressed cascades?
relations.rationale: The 2026 source applies its reported suppression to irreducible production and reheating bounds in a flat dimension; the numerical bound remains source-attributed.

relations.title: How does the conditional recoil model depend on the decay history?
relations.rationale: Compare a microscopic rate question with a conditional linear-cosmology calculation. Their targets differ; the latter does not establish that its assumed cascade occurs.

relations.title: Is the assumed repeated-decay history microscopically supported?
relations.rationale: The linear model presupposes repeated near-threshold decays. Check the applicable threshold rate without replacing the conditional calculation by a universal exclusion.

relations.title: Which initial KK population does the cosmology assume?
relations.rationale: The linear analysis inherits hot-brane production with an initially empty bulk and a specified initial temperature. This is an initial-condition route, not source equivalence.

relations.title: What linear signatures follow for a specified decaying population?
relations.rationale: Follow initial production to a distinct calculation that additionally assumes a repeated-decay history, symmetric nonrelativistic daughter kinematics and a linear regime. Production alone does not entail those premises.

relations.title: Which threshold suppression underlies the flat-model bound?
relations.rationale: Check the rate premise used by the flat-model freeze-in analysis; this reverse route does not broaden the bound to warped dimensions or other species.

relations.title: Compare inflationary mechanisms and trajectory distances
relations.qualification: Use c0 for the shared dynamics overview; this route emphasizes c1's distinct cooperative, exit, turning and trajectory/geodesic questions. The full c1 definition is unchanged. No common attractor, universal curvature sign or compulsory SDC premise is implied.
relations.rationale: The exact definitions support a differentiated next direction without presenting another indistinguishable multifield overview or merging their complete scopes.

relations.title: Examine kinetic, dissipative and gravitational mechanisms
relations.qualification: Focus on c2's stated mechanisms and their separate perturbation and exit calculations, including potential-free kinetics. General kinetic actions are not all P(φ,X), and a changed background expansion law does not supply a complete perturbation theory.
relations.rationale: c3 supplies the shared broad destination; c2 supplies a more specific comparison while preserving its action and control restrictions.

relations.title: Compare perturbation methods across kinetic actions
relations.qualification: Compare source-specific multifield methods with noncanonical and modified-gravity calculations. PyTransport's curved-metric tree-level scope does not establish support for every kinetic action; multiple-DBI horizon-exit and separable-Hubble evolution restrictions remain distinct.
relations.rationale: The existing scopes explicitly identify an action-support boundary that is useful when moving from general multifield calculations to modified dynamics.

relations.title: Study Gauss–Bonnet corrections to rapid-turn inflation
relations.qualification: Select u70's two-field inflationary question. The packet supports the target through a description and inherited introductory assessments, not its detailed formulas. No single-field inverse-potential ansatz or late-time dark-matter condition is imported.
relations.rationale: This supplies a precise gravitational-coupling question beneath the mechanism comparison while preserving the compound source's epoch split.

relations.title: Examine the source's late-time phantom conditions
relations.qualification: The target changes from two-field rapid-turn inflation to multifield late-time dark energy. The supplied late-time account requires non-negligible dark matter without direct DM–DE interaction. This is a separate announced analysis, not a demonstrated continuation of the inflationary solution.
relations.rationale: u70 explicitly contains both targets, licensing a source-linked reading route without a new physical equivalence or shared-premise claim.

relations.title: Focus on Gauss–Bonnet phantom-like dark energy
relations.qualification: Select the late-time effective equation-of-state question below -1, retaining its non-negligible-dark-matter condition and no direct DM–DE interaction. Other c5 models need not share these conditions; no wrong-sign kinetic term or observational confirmation is inferred.
relations.rationale: The existing precise c4 question supplies the phantom branch without duplicating it within the later-evolution overview.

relations.title: Isolate the Gauss–Bonnet phantom branch
relations.qualification: Select u70's multifield Gauss–Bonnet analysis, with its stated dark-matter conditions. u69's turning-dark-energy model remains a distinct question and receives no automatic phantom, dark-matter or stability conclusion.
relations.rationale: The same c4 destination is reached from the late-acceleration comparison; a second public phantom definition is unnecessary.

relations.title: Compare inflationary turning with turning dark energy
relations.qualification: Compare the early- and late-universe questions while retaining their source-specific metrics and targets. A metric differing from the flat polar example does not fix its curvature sign. Inflationary attractors, fluctuation formulas and observational tests are not transferred.
relations.rationale: c6 explicitly allows comparison with inflationary turning methods, and the supplied descriptions identify the changed epoch without establishing stronger physical relations.

relations.title: Follow a scalar–gravity model beyond inflation
relations.qualification: Use this route only for matching scalar–gravity systems. In u31, the Einstein term is retained and adding a potential is a proposed intervention tied to perturbative repair and later Einstein-dominated evolution. An inflationary fit does not establish reheating success or a universal later history.
relations.rationale: The supplied compound description connects the temporal questions while c5 preserves its distinct reheating, stiff-era, GR-attraction and dark-energy targets.

relations.title: Follow higher-point N=4 constraints toward Veneziano selection
relations.qualification: Restrict to weakly coupled, non-gravitational planar 4d EFTs with leading N=4 SYM, unbroken SU(4), massless-pole factorization and parity-even six-scalar amplitudes. Numerical selection additionally requires unitarity, analyticity, a nonzero gap and A4/s² → 0 at large |s| for fixed u < 0 or t < 0. The candidate includes four-gluon prefactors; uniqueness is unproved.
relations.rationale: c3 explicitly includes this restricted amplitude question. Both original descriptions now lead to pq0 without duplicating the destination.

relations.title: Combine dispersive bounds with independent N=4 coefficient relations
relations.qualification: This is c4's selected supersymmetric EFT branch. Symmetry, higher-point factorization and six-scalar parity first constrain coefficients without any UV-existence assumption. Only the later bootstrap adds unitarity, analyticity, a nonzero gap and the fixed-negative-u-or-t A4/s² falloff. The output remains numerical evidence for the gluon-prefactored Veneziano amplitude.
relations.rationale: c4 includes conditional combinations with independent symmetry constraints, and n77 supplies the exact specialization attribution. Parent navigation does not impose dispersion premises on the first stage.

relations.title: Compare amplitude selection with gravitational string realizability
relations.qualification: The starting question is nongravitational and concerns conditional numerical four-point selection. The destination concerns necessary gravitational consistency tests and dated string-construction comparisons in specified classes. Its restricted six-dimensional conjecture and source-specific probe assumptions remain separate; no amplitude result proves gravitational universality.
relations.rationale: n34 explicitly supports a comparison between u33 and c2. The route compares research questions without asserting containment or equivalent physical statements.

relations.title: Compare string coefficient minima with proposed consistency bounds
relations.qualification: The concrete example is leading four-graviton coefficients in toroidally compactified type II theory in D=6,7,8. Reported minima motivate future sharp-unitarity-bound tests; they are not established universal bounds or a completeness result. This route uses description and inherited attribution evidence.
relations.rationale: u58 addresses the amplitude question and has a comparison role for gravitational consistency, providing a concrete connection between the retained scopes.

relations.title: Compare symmetry and factorization constraints with dispersive bounds
relations.qualification: The overlap is selected amplitude-coefficient questions. KLT constructions, counterterm soft tests and arithmetic inequalities retain their own targets. Dispersive bounds retain source-specific growth, infrared, polarization and symmetry conditions; positivity-only and full nonlinear unitarity are distinct, and neither universal boundedness nor general transfer to gravity follows.
relations.rationale: The definitions support complementary constraint programs and a shared narrower destination pq0, while preserving their different complete scopes.

relations.title: Explore dark-matter candidates and their cosmic origins
relations.qualification: Reuse the existing candidate scope; inclusion is not certification of current viability or coverage of every compact-object proposal.
relations.rationale: Candidate construction and model–search connections form a defined direction within the dark-sector family.

relations.title: Explore extra dimensions and conditional consistency tests
relations.qualification: Construction, background and conjecture assumptions remain local to each branch.
relations.rationale: The family explicitly accommodates extra-dimensional dark sectors and conditional gravitational tests.

relations.title: What lets a relic persist, and what depletes it?
relations.qualification: Keep collective annihilation, PBH evaporation and discharge, and KK cascades distinct; some constrained relics need not supply dark matter.
relations.rationale: The existing survival question provides the shared persistence direction without identifying mechanisms.

relations.title: How is the candidate's abundance and momentum distribution produced?
relations.qualification: Thermal contact, equilibrium, stability and initial conditions remain source-specific. The production overview also includes systems beyond the candidate overview.
relations.rationale: Candidate origins lead to the existing production target without requiring scope equivalence or containment.

relations.title: Can the proposed population survive its later evolution?
relations.qualification: An initial abundance does not establish persistence; the destination also covers populations that are not dark matter.
relations.rationale: Candidate construction and later survival are connected but separate questions.

relations.title: Check extra-dimensional assumptions where invoked
relations.qualification: Follow this check only for candidates invoking the specified constructions or gravitational hypotheses; ordinary candidates acquire no such premise.
relations.rationale: The existing definitions support a conditional construction check, not a universal quantum-gravity test.

relations.title: Can a hot Standard Model brane populate a KK tower?
relations.qualification: Use the fixed Dark Dimension production assumptions, including specified temperature and bulk population. No production integral or later survival is verified.
relations.rationale: This is the source-specific gravitational production branch of the existing abundance question.

relations.title: Study hot-brane production in the Dark Dimension setup
relations.qualification: The route concerns one specified construction and its initial abundance, not every compactification or a demonstrated dark-energy mechanism.
relations.rationale: The extra-dimensional and dark-relic production entries converge on the same fixed scientific destination.

relations.title: Can KK cascades preserve a relic population?
relations.qualification: Retain the threshold, dark-matter-viability and non-dark-matter freeze-in components, with separate flat and warped qualifications.
relations.rationale: The compound KK question is the existing survival overview's focused tower branch.
